title: Functions & Graphs
source: Sullivan 10e; Aufmann, Barker & Nation 7e; additions from Axler and Stewart

children.title: Coordinate Plane
Why does the distance formula come from Pythagoras?
children.summary: Draws the right triangle between two points; the legs are Δx and Δy

children.title: Why is the midpoint an average?
children.summary: Sees halfway in x and halfway in y independently

children.title: Why is a circle (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²?
children.summary: Drags a point that stays at distance r from the centre; the distance formula becomes the equation

children.title: Why do the symmetry tests work?
children.summary: Replaces x by −x (or y by −y) and sees the mirror point land on the graph

children.title: Why is the perpendicular the shortest way to a line?
children.summary: Drags a point along the line; the distance is least where the segment meets it at 90°

children.title: Intercepts and plotting by points
children.summary: Plots from a table and finds where the graph meets the axes

children.title: Find a circle's centre from its general form
children.summary: Completes the square twice to read off the centre and radius

children.title: Lines & Slope
Why is slope the same anywhere on a line?
children.summary: Slides a rise/run triangle along the line; similar triangles keep the ratio (see Trigonometry → Similar Triangles)

children.title: Why do perpendicular slopes multiply to −1?
children.summary: Rotates a slope triangle by 90°: rise and run swap, and one changes sign

children.title: Why does a vertical line have no slope?
children.summary: Steepens a line until the run is 0 and the ratio breaks

children.title: Why does a constant rate of change make a straight line?
children.summary: Compares tables with equal steps in y and with growing steps

children.title: Why is the angle between lines tan θ = |(m₂ − m₁)/(1 + m₁m₂)|?
children.summary: Subtracts the two inclinations using tan(A − B)

children.title: Convert between forms of a line
children.summary: Edits point–slope, slope–intercept, two-point and general forms; all stay in sync

children.title: Graph a line from its equation
children.summary: Plots the intercept and then steps by the slope

children.title: Distance from a point to a line
children.summary: Uses |Ax₀ + By₀ + C|/√(A² + B²) and checks it with the perpendicular

children.title: Collinear points from slopes
children.summary: Checks whether the slopes AB and BC are equal

children.title: Linear models: fares and depreciation
children.summary: Builds C = mx + b from a story and reads the meaning of m and b

children.title: What is a Function?
Why must a function give exactly one output?
children.summary: Sees a vending machine that gives two items for one button is broken; the vertical line test is the same idea

children.title: Why do domains get restricted?
children.summary: Drags x across √, ÷ and log and watches where each one breaks

children.title: Why the difference quotient?
children.summary: Draws a secant between x and x + h; its slope is the difference quotient, and shrinking h previews calculus

children.title: Why is f(x + h) not f(x) + h?
children.summary: Compares the two on a graph for f(x) = x²

children.title: When are two functions really equal?
children.summary: Compares x and x²/x: same formula after cancelling, but different domains, so different functions

children.title: Why is a relation a subset of A × B?
children.summary: Draws the A × B grid and ticks the pairs; the grid has p·q cells

children.title: Function machine: rule, table, graph
children.summary: Sees one function shown three ways, kept in sync

children.title: Read a graph
children.summary: Reads off the domain, range, f(a) and where f(x) = c

children.title: Properties & Library
Why are even functions mirror images?
children.summary: Sees f(−x) = f(x) as a y-axis mirror, and odd functions as a half-turn about the origin

children.title: Why are turning points where max and min live?
children.summary: Traces increasing and decreasing stretches; peaks sit where the direction flips

children.title: The library of parent functions
children.summary: Browses x, x², x³, √x, ∛x, 1/x, |x| and ⌊x⌋ with their key features

children.title: Why does the greatest-integer function jump?
children.summary: Slides x across an integer and the output snaps

children.title: Piecewise-function builder
children.summary: Defines pieces on intervals and sees open and closed dots at the joins

children.title: Average rate of change
children.summary: Picks two points and reads the secant slope as an average speed

children.title: Income-tax slabs as a piecewise function
children.summary: Enters an income and sees the tax curve made of linear pieces

children.title: Transformations
Why does f(x − 2) move the graph right?
children.summary: Compares tables: the input must be 2 bigger to reach the same output (spec below)
children.spec: Table view: two tables, f(x) and f(x − 2); highlight that the output 4 now appears 2 rows later. Input dial: drag x and see the 'effective input' x − 2 lag behind it. Graph view: a ghost of f follows, and the shift slider's sign is drawn as an arrow. Contrast: f(x) − 2 alongside, where changing the output moves the graph the way you'd expect.

children.title: Why does f(2x) squeeze but 2f(x) stretch?
children.summary: Changes the input versus the output and sees horizontal changes act 'backwards'

children.title: Why does the order of transformations matter?
children.summary: Shifts then stretches, then reverses the order, and gets a different graph

children.title: −f(x) versus f(−x)
children.summary: Flips over the x-axis versus the y-axis

children.title: Transformation sequence builder
children.summary: Stacks shifts, stretches and reflections on any parent function (see Trigonometry → Sine & Cosine Graphs)

children.title: Match the graph to the equation
children.summary: Plays a timed matching game

children.title: Combining & Inverting
Why is f∘g not g∘f?
children.summary: Puts on socks then shoes, then shoes then socks, with two function machines

children.title: Why does the domain of f∘g shrink?
children.summary: Sees g's outputs that f can't accept get removed

children.title: Why must a function be one-to-one to invert?
children.summary: Sweeps a horizontal line: two hits means 'undo' is ambiguous

children.title: Why does the inverse reflect in y = x?
children.summary: Swaps every (a, b) to (b, a) and watches the graph fold (see Trigonometry → Inverses)

children.title: Why undo in reverse order?
children.summary: Sees (f∘g)⁻¹ = g⁻¹∘f⁻¹: take shoes off before socks

children.title: Why is every increasing function one-to-one?
children.summary: Slides a horizontal line across a rising graph; it can only hit once

children.title: Why is one-one the same as onto for a finite set, but not for ℕ?
children.summary: Maps 5 balls to 5 boxes (no clash forces no empty box), then maps ℕ → ℕ by n ↦ 2n (one-one, misses the odds)

children.title: Why is f⁻¹ not 1/f? (and sin⁻¹ x ≠ 1/sin x)
children.summary: Plots sin⁻¹ x and (sin x)⁻¹ = cosec x side by side: one undoes sine, the other is its reciprocal

children.title: Find an inverse algebraically
children.summary: Swaps x and y, solves, then checks on the graph

children.title: Add, subtract, multiply functions
children.summary: Combines two graphs point by point

children.title: Decompose a function
children.summary: Writes √(x² + 1) as f∘g in several ways

children.title: °C ↔ °F and currency there-and-back
children.summary: Converts and back again: an inverse pair in everyday life

children.title: Quadratic Functions
Why is the vertex at x = −b/2a?
children.summary: Sees the vertex sit midway between the roots, or wherever completing the square puts it

children.title: Why does a control direction and width?
children.summary: Slides a through negative, small and large values

children.title: Why is every parabola the same shape?
children.summary: Zooms y = ax² until it matches y = x²: all parabolas are similar

children.title: Standard ↔ vertex ↔ factored form
children.summary: Edits any one form and the others update

children.title: Find a quadratic from a vertex and a point
children.summary: Fixes the vertex, then drags a point to solve for a

children.title: Biggest field for a fixed fence
children.summary: Changes the width; area is a parabola with its peak at the square

children.title: Price that maximises revenue
children.summary: Drags the price; revenue = price × demand peaks at the vertex

children.title: Projectiles and bridge arches
children.summary: Fits a parabola to an arch or a ball's path

children.title: Polynomial Functions
Why does the leading term decide the ends?
children.summary: Zooms out until xⁿ swamps every other term

children.title: Why do some roots bounce and others cross?
children.summary: Changes the multiplicity: (x − a)² can't change sign

children.title: Why at most n roots and n − 1 turns?
children.summary: Builds a degree-n polynomial from its factors and counts

children.title: Why does the remainder theorem work?
children.summary: Plugs c into P(x) = (x − c)Q(x) + R and the first term vanishes

children.title: Why is the list of rational roots so short?
children.summary: Sees that p must divide the constant and q the leading coefficient

children.title: Descartes' rule of signs
children.summary: Counts sign changes and compares them with the actual positive roots (the rule is shown, not proved)

children.title: Why degree n means n complex roots
children.summary: Peels off one factor at a time until nothing is left (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra)

children.title: Why is there no formula past degree 4?
children.summary: Follows the story from Tartaglia and Cardano to Abel: formulas exist up to degree 4 and provably not beyond

children.title: Find every zero
children.summary: Lists candidates, uses synthetic division, then finishes with the quadratic formula

children.title: Trap a root (intermediate value theorem)
children.summary: Halves an interval where the sign changes until the root is pinned

children.title: Open-top box from a sheet
children.summary: Cuts corners of size x; the volume is a cubic with a best x

children.title: Rational Functions
Why vertical asymptotes, and when only a hole?
children.summary: Zeros the denominator: if the factor cancels you get a hole, otherwise a wall

children.title: Why do degrees decide the horizontal asymptote?
children.summary: Races the leading terms as x grows

children.title: Why a slant asymptote?
children.summary: Long division leaves a line plus a remainder that fades

children.title: Why can a graph cross a horizontal asymptote but never a vertical one?
children.summary: Sees a horizontal asymptote is only about the far ends

children.title: Analyse a rational function
children.summary: Walks through domain → intercepts → asymptotes → sign chart → sketch

children.title: Average cost falls toward a limit
children.summary: Watches cost per item = (fixed + variable·n)/n approach the variable cost

children.title: Least metal for a can
children.summary: Fixes the volume and minimises surface area over the radius

children.title: Modelling with Data
Why does 'best fit' mean least squares?
children.summary: Drags a line while the squared errors are drawn as real squares; it chases the smallest total

children.title: What does r measure?
children.summary: Sees that the correlation coefficient tracks how straight the cloud is, not how steep

children.title: Why take logs of exponential data?
children.summary: Re-plots the data on a log axis and it straightens into a line

children.title: Linear or not?
children.summary: Sorts scatter plots into linear and nonlinear

children.title: Model picker
children.summary: Fits linear, quadratic, cubic, exponential, logarithmic and logistic models to the same points and compares

children.title: Diamond price versus carat
children.summary: Fits an exponential model to the book's Hope-diamond style data

children.title: Area by Stretching
Why is a triangle half a parallelogram?
children.summary: Copies the triangle, rotates it 180° and joins them

children.title: Why does stretching by c multiply area by c?
children.summary: Stretches a region horizontally, then vertically, while a grid of squares counts the area

children.title: Why is an ellipse's area πab?
children.summary: Stretches a unit circle by a and b

children.title: Why is a circle's area πr²?
children.summary: Unrolls rings into a triangle, or cuts the disc into wedges and lays them into a near-rectangle

children.title: Area of any polygon
children.summary: Splits it into triangles
